title: Problem 02
markdown:
### Problem
In the square $ABCD$, the line from a point $E$ on side $CD$ to a point $G$ on side $BC$ is perpendicular to the diagonal $AC$ and intersects it at $F$. If $|AF| = |EG| = 20$, determine $|DE|$.

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
The length $|DE|$ is $5\sqrt{2}$.

![Figure for Jerry Heuer heuer-2022-p02-solution](study/assets/asset-heuer-2022-p02-solution-heuer-2022-p02-solution.png)

In square $ABCD$, the diagonal $AC$ makes a $45^\circ$ angle with each side: $\angle ACD = \angle ACB = 45^\circ$.

Since line $EG$ is perpendicular to diagonal $AC$ at $F$, $\angle EFC = \angle GFC = 90^\circ$.

Therefore, in right triangles $\triangle EFC$ and $\triangle GFC$:
- $\angle FCE = 45^\circ \implies \angle FEC = 45^\circ$, so $\triangle EFC$ is an isosceles right triangle with $|EF| = |FC|$.
- $\angle FCG = 45^\circ \implies \angle FGC = 45^\circ$, so $\triangle GFC$ is also an isosceles right triangle with $|GF| = |FC|$.

Thus $F$ is the midpoint of $EG$, so:

$$|EF| = |GF| = |FC| = \frac{|EG|}{2} = \frac{20}{2} = 10.$$

In the isosceles right triangle $\triangle EFC$, the hypotenuse is:

$$|EC| = \sqrt{|EF|^2 + |FC|^2} = \sqrt{10^2 + 10^2} = 10\sqrt{2}.$$

The total length of the diagonal $AC$ is:

$$|AC| = |AF| + |FC| = 20 + 10 = 30.$$

The side length of the square $CD$ is:

$$|CD| = \frac{|AC|}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{30}{\sqrt{2}} = 15\sqrt{2}.$$

Therefore:

$$|DE| = |CD| - |EC| = 15\sqrt{2} - 10\sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2}.$$

### Conceptual Explanation
Since $EG \perp AC$ and $AC$ bisects $\angle C$, $\triangle EFC$ is a $45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ$ triangle with leg $FC = EF = 10$ and hypotenuse $EC = 10\sqrt{2}$. Diagonal $AC = 20 + 10 = 30$ gives side $CD = 30/\sqrt{2} = 15\sqrt{2}$, leaving $DE = 15\sqrt{2} - 10\sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2}$.

### Key Technique
Isosceles right triangle geometry along the diagonal of a square.
